rule: docs/TREE_PLAN.md: one yard tree for every two or three houses, in back yards and at lot corners, never against a fence or a wall (zone 813 -> about 400)
written: by hand, 19 Nov 2026 (cloud session, the city-wide superchecker run from the bottom of the list). The quadrant's eighteen builder trees go (a row of jacarandas, corals, a magnolia and a ficus along the back fences, two 3 m from the house fronts, others in the yards); five come back on their own spots, about one for every two houses: by the arbor and the patio set, and in the open yards and lot corners 12 m and more from the walls.

trees.why: the back yard with the garden arbor and the patio set: a jacaranda over the table
the open lot corner at the north-east, 31 m from the walls, inside the wrought-iron fence: a full magnolia
the east yard, 12 m from the house: the yard's tree, 31 m from the corner magnolia
the middle yard by the bird of paradise, 12.5 m from the house
the west back yard of the south row, 7 m from the house: the one tree of the old back fence row (one every 6 m)
